answer: Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The umber of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, split across independent auditors, idle agents bleed standing. Each submission hangs on the pulse of a task receipt, and the shale is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit.
